thread:
ops-bot: INCIDENT detected: elevated latency on /v1/chat/completions across us-east-1. p99 crossed 2.9s for last 5m, page sent.
anya: saw the pager, looking now.
lee: I'm on traces, looks like a spike concentrated on model:mistral-8k and route:/chat/stream. Not global.
matt: any customer 5xxs?
jordan: not seeing 5xx, just slow responses. No backend errors.
anya: adding an initial mitigation — routing weight drop to mistral-8k on that pool to 0.2, failover to gptx-compat-3. Will flush prefix cache after weight change.
pd-bot: Pager acknowledged by anya.
lee: changed routing weights -> logs show policy update pushed to gateway.
ops-bot: automated metric alert suppressed for 10m because mitigation in flight.
julie: customer-impact assessment: a few power users may have increased latency; no broad degradation. No invoices impacted.
matt: timeline note: spike started ~5m before alert. Likely degraded tail responses under heavier prompt lengths.
anya: created a quick dashboard panel in the incident view for per-route p95/p99 split by model group. Sharing link: https://dashboards.internal/r/abc123 (internal)
jordan: interesting — p95 for the route is fine, p99 is ballooning only on >1024 token requests.
lee: that points to sequence-length-sensitive kernel or KV-cache issues. Could be batching policy not honoring max_length per request.
matt: agree. For now we should tune alerts so we don't page on transient, low-volume p99 blips on routes with long-seq tails.
anya: proposal: introduce "route noise-gating" — only trigger p99 page when: (1) route p99 > threshold AND (2) traffic volume in window > 30req/min OR sustained >3m, OR (3) model-group-specific p99 > threshold. This avoids pages from single long-running requests.
julie: sounds reasonable. Customers want fast reaction for real regressions but not noisy pagers.
lee: can we also use adaptive windows? e.g., for routes with <60rpm, require 10m sustained to page.
matt: yes. implement tiered gating: high-volume routes -> 1m window, medium -> 3m, low -> 10m.
ops-bot: note: alerting system supports conditional clauses and eval window. Use "traffic_volume > X" in the rule.
anya: I'll draft the alert rule change. Quick draft below:
```
alert: HighLatencyChatCompletionsPerRoute
expr: (
  > if(rate(http_requests_total{route="/chat/completions"}[1m]) > 30, histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/chat/completions"}[1m])),
  if(rate(http_requests_total{route="/chat/completions"}[5m]) > 5 and rate(http_requests_total{route="/chat/completions"}[1m]) <= 30, histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/chat/completions"}[5m])),
  histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/chat/completions"}[10m]))
) > 2.5
for: 1m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  summary: "p99 latency high for {{ $labels.route }} (model={{ $labels.model_group }})"
```
lee: nice. We should tag rule with model_group label and route so we can split per-model.
jordan: add a noise-floor check: only page if p99 - baseline_p99 > 30% to avoid small regressions on noisy routes.
matt: good call. baseline_p99 is available from the last 24h rolling baseline metric.
anya: will add that condition. Draft v2 will include baseline delta.
julie: what about p95? Should we page on p95 increase?
lee: usually p95 is more stable and better for customer-visible regressions. Let's restrict pages to p95 when there's a sustained spike across multiple routes/models (signal of platform-wide). For per-route incidents, keep p99 gating.
ops-bot: reminder: change in alert logic will also affect dashboards and runbooks; please update docs.
matt: live mitigation: we've already shifted weight. p99 returning to normal on mistral-8k pool after cache flush.
anya: saw p99 drop from 3.2s -> 1.1s over 4m after weight change. Marking incident as mitigated.
pd-bot: Incident acknowledged cleared by anya at 1919877600.
jordan: postmortem action items: 1) implement route noise-gating rules (anya) 2) create per-route-per-model p99 baseline panels (lee) 3) add automated after-action notes to incident runbook (matt) 4) evaluate batching window behavior for long sequences (>1024) (infra)
anya: I'll open a GH issue and link the alert PR.
lee: I'll create the dashboard panels and add an alert-playbook snippet for on-call.
infra: I'll investigate batching/kernel selection for long sequences and report back in 48h.
julie: I'll draft the customer-impact summary for docs and cs.
matt: one more tweak — add a soft-squelch for dev-tier routes (non-prod tags) so dev noise doesn't inflate baselines.
anya: ok. Adding dev-tier filter to rules.
lee: thanks all. Let's keep the rollouts small and monitor for 24h.
ops-bot: follow-up: created ticket #CI-4237 for rule rollout and #DASH-881 for dashboard panels.
anya: closing thread as mitigated, keeping follow-ups in tickets. :white_check_mark:
